title: [AAFLOW+] Stateful Operator Abstraction with Zero-Copy Distributed KV Cache Orchestration for Multi-Agent Workflows
event_hint: AAFLOW+: distributed KV cache orchestration system for multi-agent LLM workflows
problem: Multi-agent LLM systems remain text-centric, requiring downstream agents to repeatedly recompute shared context through expensive prefill even when identical model state was already computed by upstream agents, causing increased TTFT, duplicated computation, and poor branch factor scalability for long-context workloads
mechanism: Stateful operator abstraction extending AAFLOW from dataflow to stateflow, treating KV cache as a first-class distributed systems object with operators for materialization, transfer, fork, restricted composition, and eviction; runtime uses zero-copy communication, Arrow-based formats, explicit metadata, and transfer-aware scheduling to enable efficient KV state transfer between distributed components

evidence.claim: Stateful execution reduces TTFT by up to 50.2× at long context (from abstract; baseline unspecified in visible evidence)
evidence.condition: long context; baseline text-based orchestration unspecified in front evidence

evidence.claim: Stateful execution achieves up to 7.63× reduced multi-agent latency at 16-agent scale (from abstract; workload and hardware conditions unspecified in visible evidence)
evidence.condition: 16-agent scale; workload and hardware unspecified in front evidence

evidence.claim: Reduces peak KV memory by 1.72–6.10× (from abstract; workload and hardware conditions unspecified in visible evidence)
evidence.condition: workload and hardware unspecified in front evidence

evidence.claim: Improves throughput by more than 7.74× (from abstract; workload and hardware conditions unspecified in visible evidence)
evidence.condition: workload and hardware unspecified in front evidence

evidence.claim: Evaluation conducted on GPU clusters using Mistral-7B and Llama-3-8B models
evidence.condition: GPU cluster deployment; Mistral-7B and Llama-3-8B models

evaluation_context: GPU clusters; Mistral-7B and Llama-3-8B models; multi-agent workflows (planner-retriever-solver, tree-of-thought, collaborative RAG); comparison against text-based agent communication; analytical cost model parameterized by empirical hardware microbenchmarks
limitations: Evidence pack contains only abstract/intro/early design (front-evidence-v2); detailed evaluation sections with exact baseline conditions, hardware specifications, network bandwidth parameters, workload configurations, and complete experimental methodology are not visible in current evidence; performance claims are based on analytical cost model parameterized by empirical hardware microbenchmarks; scope focuses on multi-agent workflows rather than single-request optimization; compatibility requirements may limit state reuse (model identity, positional encoding, execution history must match)
project_relevance: Directly addresses TPN questions about state-aware scheduling reducing TTFT/TPOT and KVCache transmission overhead; KV transfer over moderate-to-high bandwidth networks vs recomputation decision criterion (Equation 7) is network-aware; zero-copy distributed KV cache orchestration provides network-side mechanisms beyond pure GPU memory scheduling; project asks whether network perceives KVCache location and Token performance targets—AAFLOW+ makes KV placement and transfer explicit in distributed execution graph

evidence_gaps.question: What are the exact baseline conditions, hardware specifications, network bandwidth, and workload configurations for the reported TTFT 50.2×, latency 7.63×, memory 1.72-6.10×, and throughput 7.74× improvements?
What are the specific network bandwidth thresholds and transfer costs where KV transfer outperforms recomputation (cited as moderate-to-high bandwidth)?
What are the exact network utilization, KVCache transmission volumes, and end-to-end P95 metrics for the multi-agent workflows?
